Name: ca-200
Title: Over 200 VR Systems in California Libraries
Description: XRLibraries began in 2016 by installing more than 200 virtual reality systems in California public libraries. Its website calls this the largest VR installation in public libraries.

Name: mission
Title: XR Made Easy for Everyone
Description: XRLibraries works with schools and libraries to bring virtual, augmented and mixed reality into their programs and classes. Its stated goal is equitable access to immersive technology for all communities.
Quote: We make XR easy to use for everyone.

Name: headset
Title: A Library VR Headset
Description: Standalone headsets let a library visitor stand on the moon, swim a coral reef or practice a job, with no computer attached. Meta Quest and Pico both appear on XRLibraries’ partner list, and its Nevada headsets run on Pico.
Partners: Meta Quest and Pico are listed partners

Name: nv-2017
Title: Nevada Follows Marin County
Description: In 2017 Nevada’s state library put its first VR headsets in public libraries: 22 headsets in 11 libraries, with STEM content. WorkingNation reports that the model followed a program at the Marin County Free Library in California.

Name: cil-talks
Title: XR at Computers in Libraries
Description: XRLibraries’ executive director, John MacLeod, presented “Integrating XR Tech & Programming in Libraries” at Computers in Libraries Connect in 2020 and “Using XR to Discover ‘Lost Stories’ & Pop-Up Books” in 2022.

Name: sandi
Title: Project SANDI
Description: Supporting and Advancing Nevada’s Dislocated Individuals began during the 2020 downturn with a $13.8 million federal grant. It uses VR to explore careers in five fields: skilled trades, healthcare, IT, advanced manufacturing and logistics.
More: The program grew to more than 1,000 headsets at over 80 locations, with 35 VR field trips and five training simulations, including dialysis technician and certified nursing assistant. XRLibraries’ executive director is a partner in the project.
Partners: Nevada Governor’s Office of Economic Development, XRLibraries

Name: nv-1100
Title: 1,100 Headsets in Nevada
Description: XRLibraries and Lifeliqe installed VR headsets in Nevada’s community college and public libraries. XRLibraries’ homepage counts more than 1,100.
More: XRLibraries uses ArborXR to set up headsets and send updates remotely. Its director told ArborXR the switch cut the time and resources spent by about 60 percent.
Where: Nevada community college and public libraries

Name: dialysis
Title: Training From a Town of 300
Description: A remote 12-week dialysis technician certification lets people train without traveling to a training center. In a community of about 300 people, a single mother finished the program, passed her certification and plans to become a registered nurse.
Quote: It brought the dialysis concepts to life.
QuoteBy: Natasha York, former library assistant, in WorkingNation

Name: playbooks
Title: XR Playbooks
Description: XRLibraries catalogs more than 300 XR apps in categories from astronomy and history to mindfulness and music, then bundles them into themed playbooks that come pre-installed on library headsets.

Name: showcase
Title: XR Showcase
Description: In this video series, hosts George and Camila try VR and AR apps for libraries, from Tilt Brush and Wander to Apollo 11 VR, and share practical tips like cleaning headsets and setting a guardian boundary.
More: Episodes also cover running big VR events with rotating stations, recording video inside a headset and playing media through the Meta Quest TV app.

Name: way-out
Title: A Way Out of No Way
Description: Marin City students who call themselves the Marinovators built a VR experience of the World War II shipyards and life in Marin City, plus a musical tribute to the African-American workers whose stories were rarely told.
More: The project ran in three tracks: immersive storytelling, music and VR modeling. It is part of XRLibraries’ Lost Stories work, which plans to look for Latino, Asian-Pacific and Native American stories next.

Name: charleston
Title: The Black Wall Street of Charleston
Description: Career and technical education students at Burke High School built an augmented-reality scavenger hunt that leads players to Charleston’s Black-owned businesses.
Partners: Burke High School CTE students, Preservation Society of Charleston, Burke High School Foundation

Name: seeking
Title: Seeking Immortality
Description: A browser-based VR world, funded by an IMLS Native American Enhancement Grant, that preserves endangered Cheyenne language and cultural knowledge. Tribal members and students learned 3D scanning so the tribe keeps control of its own data.
Partners: Northern Cheyenne Tribe, SJSU School of Information

Name: ukraine
Title: Children Draw War, Not Flowers
Description: An immersive 3D exhibition of art by children in Ukraine’s Cherkasy region, which took in more than 42,000 displaced children. It helps children work through war-related trauma, preserves their artwork, and was honored at the Anthem Awards.
Partners: SJSU School of Information, Ukrainian librarians, children and veterans, 40 regional libraries

Name: pollinators
Title: Pollinators at the Marin County Fair
Description: At XRLibraries’ bug-themed booth, fairgoers used an AR app called Pollinators to plant flowers and release monarch butterflies that flew around pollinating them. Marin artist Cynthia Jensen lent bug sculptures for the booth.

Name: freedom
Title: Freedom to Read
Description: A VR environment that helps citizens, librarians and students fight book bans, and helps young people in affected areas find challenged books that reflect their lives. It is one of the shared worlds listed on XRLibraries’ metaverse page.
Partners: SJSU School of Information, Unite Against Book Bans, Little Free Library, Books Unbanned

Name: lib-globe
Title: The Globe
Description: A terrestrial globe on a brass stand. Every library kept one long before anyone could look a place up in a second: it is the original way to see where a story is set. The places in the books on these shelves are all on it somewhere.

Name: lib-desk
Title: The Reference Desk
Description: Where you ask. Librarians were the first search engine: this is the desk where a question gets answered, a book gets found and a visitor gets pointed the right way. Nobody has ever been turned away from one for not knowing what they were looking for.
Where: The Reading Room, by the hall

Name: lib-table-north
Title: The North Reading Table
Description: A long oak table under three green-shaded banker's lamps. The lamps throw their light down on to the page and keep it out of your eyes, which is why reading rooms have used them for over a century. Sit anywhere: the chairs are leather and the table is meant to be leaned on.

Name: lib-table-south
Title: The South Reading Table
Description: The second of the room's two reading tables, a mirror of the first across the hall. Rooms like this were built so that anyone could walk in off the street and sit down with a book for nothing, which is the oldest promise a public library makes.

Name: lib-piano
Title: The Grand Piano
Description: A grand piano with its lid propped open, turned so the keyboard faces the room. Libraries have always been about more than books: lectures, readings, recitals. The lid is up because a grand is meant to be heard across a room this size, and the bench is out because someone was just playing.

Name: lib-stair
Title: The Spiral Stair
Description: Nineteen treads winding round a brass newel, up to the gallery that runs right round the room. The upper shelves are up there. Go on up: the handrail climbs with you, and the gallery is wide enough to walk the whole way round and look down on the hall.

Name: lib-window
Title: The Arched Window
Description: The room's one great window, set in the west wall so the afternoon sun comes straight down the hall. Reading rooms were laid out this way before electric light: the tables sit where the daylight falls. Beyond the glass are the hills.

Name: lib-gallery
Title: The Gallery
Description: You made it up. The gallery runs round all four walls behind a panelled parapet, with the upper shelves at your shoulder and the whole hall laid out below: the checkered floor, the runner, the chandeliers at eye level. The quietest seat in the building is the one you are standing in.
Where: The Reading Room, up the spiral stair

Name: wax-2016
Title: The First Headsets
Description: In 2016, libraries in Marin County, California, began offering virtual reality stations as the pilot for the California Virtual Reality Experience. XRLibraries launched that year as the project’s coordinator. Teen volunteers helped first-time visitors into headsets and guided them through their first worlds.
More: Library Journal reported that four Marin County libraries had offered VR stations since 2016, with teens from the Marin WebStars volunteer program helping manage the stations and guide new users.
Partners: Califa, Marin County Free Library, XRLibraries

Name: wax-2017a
Title: VR Goes Statewide
Description: In June 2017 the California State Library, Oculus and the library consortium Califa partnered to bring VR-ready PCs with Rift headsets to more than 90 libraries across California, building on the Marin County pilot. XRLibraries, launched in 2016 as the project’s coordinator, also became a clearinghouse where libraries share what works with VR and AR.
More: XRLibraries’ website counts more than 200 VR systems installed in California public libraries, and calls it the largest VR installation in public libraries.

Name: wax-2017b
Title: Story Time in 3D
Description: Library Journal reported in 2017 that young children loved virtual reality story times, while teens gravitated to VR games. In Marin, children listened to stories inside three-dimensional worlds.
Partners: Libraries in the California Virtual Reality Experience

Name: wax-2018a
Title: Nevada Opens Its Stations
Description: Nevada’s state library set aside $22,000 of a 2017 budget increase for a VR pilot: 22 headsets loaded with STEM content in 11 libraries, modeled on Marin County’s program. In February 2018 the Carson City Library’s grand re-opening featured VR and AR stations, and XRLibraries’ founder presented in a webinar for librarians across the state.
Where: Carson City Library and other Nevada libraries

Name: wax-2019a
Title: VR on the Road
Description: Marin’s VR program went out into the community: to schools, senior centers, the county fair, and people displaced by deadly wildfires.

Name: wax-2019b
Title: VR in the World’s Catalog
Description: Nevada’s state library and its partner XRLibraries set out to catalog VR content so any library could find it. In 2019 Nevada librarians led a first-of-its-kind effort to catalog virtual reality in WorldCat, the world’s largest library catalog, and planned a cataloging hack-a-thon in Marin, California and Carson City, Nevada.
More: Nevada’s Governor’s Office of Economic Development says a Carson City librarian cataloged the first VR course companion in WorldCat, and that the work produced a collection of more than 1,000 3D interactive VR objects.

Name: wax-2019c
Title: XR Marin and the XR Stars
Description: XR Marin brought together the Marin County Free Library, XRLibraries, Novato Unified School District and the Marin County Office of Education. Teens served as “XR Stars,” helping patrons use the equipment. Its programs let people make 3D models, design 3D games and produce 360-degree video tours, and one teen at a VR summer camp borrowed the cameras and filmed her family’s farm.
Partners: Marin County Free Library, XRLibraries, Novato Unified School District, Marin County Office of Education

Name: wax-2020
Title: Project SANDI
Description: In October 2020 Nevada won a $13.8 million federal grant for Project SANDI (Supporting and Advancing Nevada’s Dislocated Individuals), which uses VR to explore careers in skilled trades, healthcare, IT, advanced manufacturing and logistics. It grew to more than 1,000 headsets at over 80 locations. XRLibraries’ executive director is a partner in the project.
Partners: Nevada Governor’s Office of Workforce Innovation, Governor’s Office of Economic Development, Nevada libraries and colleges

Name: wax-2022a
Title: 360° Stories in Washington
Description: XRLibraries was the trainer for the Washington State Library’s VR 360 grant program. In 2022 it helped six libraries create 360-degree virtual reality stories about topics important to their communities. The program was open to public, tribal and academic libraries and funded by IMLS through the Library Services and Technology Act.

Name: wax-2022b
Title: Lost Stories
Description: In Marin City, students who call themselves the Marinovators built a VR experience of the World War II shipyards and life in Marin City, plus a musical tribute to the African-American workers whose stories were rarely told. XRLibraries’ director presented its Lost Stories work at Computers in Libraries in 2022.
More: The project ran in three tracks: immersive storytelling, music and VR modeling.

Name: wax-2024
Title: Children Draw War, Not Flowers
Description: XRLibraries helped design “Children Draw War, Not Flowers,” a browser-based VR art exhibition from the San José State University School of Information. It shows art by Ukrainian children aged 4 to 16 and virtual galleries showing the destruction of Ukrainian libraries, and anyone can visit it free in a web browser.
More: XRLibraries lists the exhibition, which was honored at the Anthem Awards, among its shared worlds.
Partners: SJSU School of Information, Ukrainian librarians and children

Name: wax-2025
Title: Pollinators at the Fair
Description: At the 2025 Marin County Fair, XRLibraries’ bug-themed booth featured Pollinators, an augmented-reality app where fairgoers planted flowers and released monarch butterflies that flew around pollinating them. Marin artist Cynthia Jensen lent bug sculptures for the booth.
